get.description: Open, no key needed. `503` with `status: "degraded"` when the workflow engine is unreachable: in that state no payment can start, so point your load balancer and uptime monitor here.
Open, no key needed. The live corridors and the status of every feature on this environment. Fetch it at startup and gate your integration on it rather than hard-coding a corridor list.

get.summary: Who this API key belongs to
get.description: Your organization, your role and, for a member key, which member you are. No side effects, so it is also the honest way to check that a key works.

post.description: Prices a payment without starting one. Returns a single-use `quoteId` that locks the rate for about a minute; pass it to `POST /transactions` to pay exactly this price. Supply `idempotencyKey` (the future payment ID) to bind the quote to that payment.

422.description: Understood, but cannot be done as asked: no_route_for_chain, not_home_wallet, quote_unavailable

post.description: Starts a durable payment and answers `202` straight away. Your `idempotencyKey` becomes the transaction ID: retrying the same request never pays twice. Funded from your home wallet. Follow it with `GET /transactions/:id` or webhooks.

422.description: Understood, but cannot be done as asked: ambiguous_home_wallet, insufficient_funds, no_home_wallet, not_home_wallet, quote_expired, quote_mismatch, quote_not_found, wallet_chain_unknown

get.description: Newest first, cursor-paginated. Rows are what you submitted; read each row's live status from `GET /transactions/:id`.
A payment that is not yours is `404`, the same as one that does not exist.

404.description: Not found, or not yours: not_found

post.description: Up to 1,000 payments to one corridor on one rail, funded from your home wallet in a single transfer. A batch is accepted or refused **as a whole**; once accepted, each item is paid independently and can fail on its own. Counts against the `initiate` rate limit **once per item**.

400.description: Invalid request: duplicate_item_ref, invalid_send_amount, unknown_recipient, validation

get.summary: Where to send USDC on chain, and what each network costs
get.description: Your deposit address on every network we credit. USDC sent on your home network is credited as it is; USDC sent on any other network is moved to your home network and the `fee` for that is deducted. Each non-home network carries a live fee estimate.
